minor: The chart line reads 'After that outcry, the loss of about 800,000 US subscribers in the third quarter of 2011 followed'. Qwikster was dropped on 10 October, after the quarter ended on 30 September. The sourced cause is the July price rise plus the Qwikster announcement. Reword to 'In the third quarter of 2011, about 800,000 US subscribers left after the price rise, with the Qwikster announcement on top.'
'Years of free streaming' in the closing cost line is loose. Streaming was included in the plan at no extra fee, but it was not free to members. 'Years of streaming at no extra fee' is more exact.
'That January, Hastings had stepped back' follows the 29 September 2023 line, so 'that January' is ambiguous. Say 'In January 2023'.
The Starz 2011 fee line comes before the August 2010 Epix line, so the order is not chronological. It changes no fact.
Apple's iTunes movies were purchases at launch and Amazon Unbox offered rentals too, so 'to keep' is slightly loose for both.
'Nearly a year's profit': $40M against $49M is about 82%. Acceptable, but 'most of a year's profit' is safer.
The Dallas offer is told only from Randolph's account, which the script credits. Keep that attribution.
